title: Visit, lab and drug-screen intervals for Prescriptions & Renewals classes
content:
**Medication Management Office standard — monitoring intervals.** For each class of the Prescriptions & Renewals line this schedule gives the calendar months after the patient's most recent completed visit with the prescribing department within which a renewal may be approved without a new visit, the calendar months after the last monitoring lab and after the last drug screen within which a renewal may be approved, and the days past the estimated run-out of the last fill beyond which a renewal needs prescriber review even under the refill protocol.

| Class | Visit interval (calendar months) | Monitoring lab interval (calendar months) | Drug screen interval (calendar months) | Adherence gap for prescriber review (days past run-out) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acute Short-Course Prescription | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Standard Maintenance Prescription | 12 | 0 | 0 | 60 |
| Monitored Maintenance Prescription | 6 | 6 | 0 | 30 |
| Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription | 6 | 0 | 12 | 30 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 3 | 0 | 6 | 14 |
| Specialty Medication Prescription | 6 | 3 | 0 | 30 |

**Zero entries.** A monitoring lab interval of 0 means the class has no monitoring labs; a drug screen interval of 0 means no drug screen is required; an adherence gap of 0 means that review point does not apply. The Acute Short-Course Prescription carries 0 in every column of this schedule.

**Reading across a row.** The Monitored Maintenance Prescription is the only class with both a visit interval and a lab interval of 6 months; the Specialty Medication Prescription pairs a 6-month visit interval with a 3-month lab interval; the controlled classes carry a drug screen interval instead of a lab interval — 12 months for Schedule III-V and 6 months for Schedule II.
